messages:
alex: Heads-up — customer (StellarApps) hit a spike of 504s on streaming generate yesterday evening. They say SDK v1.4 auto-retries and they end up paying for duplicate tokens. sample request id: rq_0a3bf9e2, region=us-west2.

maria: Thanks. Do we have exact timestamps + correlation ids? Is this only streaming or non-stream too?

alex: Only streaming so far. Timestamps in their logs: 2025-02-18T21:06:12Z (initial), reset at 2025-02-18T21:06:24Z, sdk retry at 21:06:24.250. They see ~3 retries in quick succession. model=redwood/standard-13b, quant=8, prefix_cache=true.

customer-bob: Confirming — we see the connection drop consistently ~11-13s into the stream. SDK then retries immediately and we get billed for both. Very visible in our monthly bill.

devlin-eng-runtime: Possible angle: edge -> gateway keepalive mismatch or backend eviction when KV cache rehydration hits a lock. Need proxies' logs for stream ID x-forwarded-stream-id. Can you paste full request headers (redact tokens)?

alex: Pasted headers (redacted):
```
:method: POST
:path: /v1/generate/stream
:authority: api.redwood.example
user-agent: stellar-sdk/1.4
authorization: Bearer REDACTED
x-region: us-west2
x-forwarded-stream-id: 0x7b2f3a
```

maria: Noted. @jordan-sre can you check edge connection reset metrics for that stream id window? Also flag if we saw sudden spike in active connections from that customer (could be thundering herd due to retries).

jordan-sre: I see a burst at 21:06:24Z from that customer IP range — simultaneous reconnect attempts. Edge logs show RST_STREAM followed by 504 from gateway. Opening a pod-level trace now.

sre-bot: deploybot: rolling restart of gw-proxy/us-west2 started at 2025-02-18T22:10:00Z (not related to this window but FYI).

devlin-eng-runtime: Two hypotheses: 1) upstream backend closes the stream on KV cache lock/timeout and gateway translates to 504, 2) edge TCP keepalive timeout causing abrupt reset while gateway still has inflight. Both can cause immediate client retry loops -> duplicate billing. We'll instrument additional tracing.

sara-support: Drafting an update to the customer. Suggested messaging: apologize, explain investigative steps, recommended temporary client mitigations (set maxRetries=2, add jitter/backoff, increase streaming timeout to 30s). Any objections?

alex: sounds good. Also advise to enable client-side idempotency key for non-streaming calls if possible. For streaming, recommend disabling automatic retries while we root cause.

customer-bob: Disabling retries would break our UX. Can you throttle us server-side or route to a lower-concurrency pool? We can accept slightly lower throughput to avoid double bills.

devlin-eng-runtime: We can pin their requests to a dedicated low-concurrency pool as a temporary mitigation — requires infra touch but doable. I'll check capacity.

jordan-sre: From metrics: gateway 5xx rate for that minute jumped to 6% for us-west2, connection reset count +420. We'll correlate with backend pod OOM/kvcache lock logs.

alex: I attached the customer's minimal repro steps in the support ticket (stream a 3k-token prompt, leave open, observe 11-13s drop). They can share a packet capture if OK.

devlin-eng-runtime: Requesting eng-runtime oncall to run targeted trace for x-forwarded-stream-id 0x7b2f3a and the req id rq_0a3bf9e2. Also will add counters for "stream-close-reason" on gateway to break out keepalive vs backend-close vs proxy-reset.

sara-support: Customer update sent. Quick note: included the temporary SDK settings and offered dedicated routing while we triage.

jordan-sre: Follow-up: found backend log lines showing "kv-cache lock timeout for session xyz" at 21:06:23Z, then connection closed by backend at 21:06:24Z. Seems aligned.

devlin-eng-runtime: That matches hypothesis 1. Next steps: change kv-cache lock timeout to be more permissive for streaming workloads and add non-blocking eviction path. Will ship a canary to a single host in us-west2; ETA 4 hours.

sara-support: I'll keep the customer informed and offer to backdate billing credits for duplicate tokens if this is confirmed.

alex: After canary, please post results here. If canary reduces stream closes to zero in the window, we can roll forward.

customer-bob: Appreciate the responsiveness. Please ping when you want us to test.

devlin-eng-runtime: Canary deployed to host gw-uw2-canary-7 at 02:15 UTC. Instrumented with extra logging.

jordan-sre: Early read: stream-close events dropped 92% on the canary host in the same repro workload.

sara-support: Customer notified, they will run an ingress test in 20 minutes.

customer-bob: Test done — no resets observed in 30 minutes. Looks good so far.

alex: Closing loop after 24h stable. Follow-up action items: make kv-cache lock non-blocking for streaming, add opt-in server-side per-customer low-concurrency routing, and update SDK docs on default retry behavior for streaming.

maria: Filed follow-up tickets and assigned owners. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
